blurb: A backslash in a string literal starts an escape, and this one is not in the set: `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`, `\"`, `\\`, `\u{…}` (1 to 6 hex digits in braces) and `\(…)` for interpolation. To write a backslash itself, double it, as in a Windows path. A `\u{…}` naming a surrogate or a value past U+10FFFF is `bynk.lex.bad_unicode_escape`.
example:
const Dir: String = "C:\Users"      // ✗ `\U` is not an escape
const Dir: String = "C:\\Users"     // ✓ a doubled backslash
summary: An invalid escape sequence in a string literal.
